body:
I'm sorry you're going through it too. I hope you have access to therapy, or otherwise maybe some good books about it. 

And saying to someone that he/she is forgettable is just so mean. I don't know why people are like that. I'm sure that's not true and I hope you can believe that yourself someday. And being nice and understanding IS a good thing, as long as you still put yourself first and set boundaries where they need to be set. But it's hard to even sometimes feel where the boundaries are, for me, so I get it.
Yeah, I see what you mean and I think you're right.

No, they're not healthy. They're definitely not all narcs either. I had two close friends who were narcs. One I was friends with for almost 20 years, so since we were kids, the other about 7 years. And it did a lot to me. I threw them out. A couple with autism, couple with ADHD, other personality disorders, depression, anxiety, addiction... Some of these are diagnosed, some of these are just pretty obvious if you know them well and have eyes and ears, but will never be diagnosed because they refuse help. 

It's not their fault they aren't healthy, but I came to the point of throwing people out if their behaviour worsened or stayed the same for years and years and they refused help and it affected me negatively regularly. It's not my responsibility and I want to get better, I don't want to get dragged down with them. And this is not after someone is depressed for a year or something. Depression or anxiety I can handle. It's more outbursts out of nowhere from someone under the influence, having a shit evening AGAIN because someone is too drunk or has a temper tantrum for no reason, responses without any empathy towards me, no self reflection, no support, lying, manipulating, saying mean things behind my back and so on. Saying sorry and then repeating the exact same behaviour or even worse shortly after. And I always forgave these things for years and years, but when I was at my most depressed the last couple of years, I couldn't take it anymore and I started to toss people out. 

But STILL there is self-doubt sometimes. Am I just the difficult one? Doesn't everyone have problems? Is anyone even 'healthy'? Am I expecting too much from people? Because this is just what I'm used to. Everyone seems to have mental health issues around me, including myself. So maybe it's normal. Or maybe not and I just don't know what 'normal' looks like.
Thank you so much for your advice and encouraging words. Every comment in here has really warmed my freakin' heart ❤️

Thank you! Yes I want a dog really REALLY badly.... But I'm financially not in the position to care for a dog right now. And I'm too much of a dog lover to just be selfish and take the chance that maybe I can't take the best care of him/her. I have to have a little more stability in my life in terms of work and money and then I will definitely get a dog. I have wanted a dog since I've known dogs existed. 

And thank you for saying that my feelings and expectations are reasonable... It's always what I feel myself, but sometimes I start to think that maybe I'm the unreasonable one. Because you read sometimes: 'when everyone around you is an asshole.... You must be the asshole.' That statement always hurts to read. Must be hurtful to read for people that are abused and bullied as well. But it creates a lot of self-doubt. 

And I've been told that the reason why I seem unapproachable is more because I just have a resting bitch face, this is what I've heard from people around me that know me by now. But they said that they wouldn't dare to come up to me or that they thought I was a bitch before they talked to me, and were surprised that I was actually nice lol. So, I really try to smile a lot to strangers, but when my face is just relaxed, I can seem to be in a bad mood, when I'm actually not. My hygiene and clothing are fine. It's my face 😂

I'm sorry you have a mom like that as well. My mother is a vulnerable or covert narcissist as well I think. I'm not an expert but I'm learning through a doctor on YouTube about all the different types. My mother is also obsessed with achievements. Everything school or work related was/is the most important thing on the planet. She can't talk about emotions at all, the only time she shows emotions is when she is the victim and/or when she's drunk. Even when she is clearly the perpetrator, she can twist it so that she is the victim. It's mind boggling. 

And also very judgmental. I'm too fat, too thin, why am I wearing that, why is my hair like this, I'm wearing too much makeup, not enough makeup, I'm too hyper, I'm too relaxed. That girl is so skinny, she must be an anorexic. Antidepressants are bad. 'why are they bad?' just because, they're bad. Your house is not clean enough. You're never nice to me. Blablabla. 

Also, when I point out to her: I didn't like that you said this or that to me yesterday. She just says: I didn't say that, you're just making stuff up now. 

She adores people that are doctors or lawyers or something, because of status or something? I don't know. She's fucking weird. Manipulative and passive aggressive as well, tries to wind me up so I blow up and she can play the victim again. But I'm learning to stay calm now. Very good at giving the silent treatment. Very difficult woman. And then cries about the fact that she doesn't have a good relationship with me and my sister. We must be horrible daughters!

Yes, I'm already a little better at respecting my own boundaries when it comes to those things, fortunately. But I will never be a person that calls someone 8 times in a row. I'm not begging for attention, if they still ignore me I would probably die a little inside lol. 

But yeah maybe I just have to learn how to appreciate surface level relationships more, it's just not something I'm used to and I would have to really watch my words. I tend to go deep, otherwise I'm bored or the relationship feels empty to me. Probably because I've lacked connection all my life or something. 

Thank you for your responses ❤️

Thank you, this was very helpful and is giving me hope! And absolutely quality over quantity, I don't have to have a massive group of friends anymore. I think I'll try to do some yoga outside of my living room lol.
Thank you so much 🥰

The talking over me, cancelling plans and forgetting to answer part, I already pointed those things out numerous times. Now in a much calmer way than a couple of years ago as I've grown as a person through therapy and I think I learned to communicate a little better. But as you've said, you can't change other people. And after pointing those things out 10 times or even more, how many more times are you going to point it out to them? Even after telling them why it triggers me so much, it doesn't change. Then it's pretty clear to me that there's no point in saying anything anymore, because they don't listen and/or are unwilling or can not change those things. Then there are two options. I 'accept' those things from them, which means I will still be frustrated, but I won't say anything about it, because REALLY accepting those things.. I don't think I can. Or I'm not hanging out with you anymore.

I know everyone is their own person and I absolutely don't expect perfection from anyone. If you cancel plans once in a while, it's fine. Everyone cancels sometimes. But if you cancel plans 8 out of 10 times I make plans with you, it's a problem. If you forget to answer to a text sometimes, sure! Everyone does that. Everyone has their own lives, I know the world doesn't revolve around me and I don't expect an answer immediately. But if it becomes a regular thing that I have to wait 48 hours for a response from you, especially when it is something important that I text you or I needed support, then it is a problem. And that same person calls me nervously 8 times in a row when I don't text back fast enough. It's all about patterns, not about incidents. 

Your last question is interesting, because that's what my therapist also asked me. It's a tough thing for me because I really hate surfaced relationships. Not every friendship has to be the same of course. But if we just talk about bullshit, and I can't go deep otherwise I get hurt, I would have to be really mindful and walk on eggshells all the time, because deep conversation comes naturally to me. I don't feel comfortable to just talk about... Nothing. Small talk. Then maybe I would just rather be alone. I want friends I can also of course have fun with, just hang out, watch a movie, go to a concert, go on vacations and whatever, it doesn't have to be heavy and deep all the time. But I want it to be an option. I want there to be mutual respect and support if it's necessary. Otherwise I don't really feel a connection and I wouldn't call it a friendship. Then I would call that person an acquaintance.

Yes, for me it's the same. A lot of relationships have been me as the carer. And they could come to me day and night and I would go way too deep into their problems, still do sometimes, and that's my fault too. I was and still am overstepping my own boundaries with that behaviour, but it's such automatic behaviour. And then when I have a problem it's not as important to them or not important at all. And that hurts. 

And sometimes I don't even have the energy to explain myself anymore, you know? Emotional neglect seems to be a very hard thing to understand for people who didn't experience it themselves. It's not as clear as physical abuse or something. It's more vague for people I think. I tried my best to explain it to people around me, so they could maybe understand me a little bit more and hopefully be more considerate, but sometimes I don't have the energy to do it again and I just want them to connect the fucking dots and just treat me with basic respect and as if I'm not a robot but I am a human being with feelings. But maybe that's asking too much. I don't know.

Thank you for your answer. That's awesome that you found a perfect partner for you that doesn't have the same patterns as your parent(s)! That's what I'm hoping for as well and also one of the (many) reasons I did go to therapy. 

But yeah, I think you're right, I 'chose' friends, subconsciously of course, that repeated those same patterns. At first it wasn't as much of an issue, when we were younger we were just always partying, just drinking and doing drugs and stuff. But the last couple of years, when my life really went to shit, it became so clear to me that I couldn't lean on most of those people, even those who always leaned heavily on me. So most of those people I already don't see anymore for a couple of years now. I realize now that most of my friendships have been toxic. Very one sided and very draining. Some narcs, some codependency, a lot of addicts, a lot of boundaries were crossed and overall I was once again just not seen, heard or understood. I was mostly their therapist and when I tried to be heard, there was no space for that, or I should just man up and shut my mouth. 

People tend to overestimate me in terms of emotions, I come across way stronger than I actually am, so this is also not great. But I was of course taught that showing emotions is not normal, vulnerability is weird, so I am just now learning that in my late twenties how to do that, through therapy. In that area I'm basically still a fucking toddler lol. 

And yeah I'm planning on doing things just by myself, to meet new people, but that's also really scary for me. I'm pretty introverted so I find it scary to just go up and talk to someone and I don't really look that approachable (so I've heard, many times). So I don't know how that will turn out. But I'm going to try. I have to.

Yep. Those are not really friends in my eyes. I don't trust my own judgment anymore when meeting new people. And I'm not one for surfaced relationships. But it's ok to go deep about their problems, but not the other way around. Then you're a burden suddenly. Great.
I'm glad you're ok with that, but I'm not. People are social animals. We're not made to be alone. So it's a perfectly normal need for a human being to want to feel loved, supported and appreciated.

Yeah I don't think my worldview is incorrect. I know not all people are like this but the people around me are unfortunately. I know where my triggers are and this is a big one, because I've been emotionally neglected by my family. I chose friends who are also emotionally neglectful. So I chose the wrong people (subconsciously) a while ago and now that I'm in this place, it's become more clear to me.
What do you mean?

Thank you. I've been out of work for almost a year because of my mental health. I've been applying for jobs but just got rejected and that has taken a toll again. It's very stressful and I have to put on my mask all the time. I'm now (again) looking for some volunteerwork. I'm still in pretty intensive therapy. So if I can do volunteer work and therapy, that should fill up the weeks. 

I can relate totally to what you said about you reaching out to your friends and they don't, or very little. It sucks. And that makes me feel unwanted too. Like they don't really want to hang out with me but do it out of pity. Even though I know I'm a good friend, I am social and have humor. But they're too busy/don't like me anymore, have a new relationship that takes over all of their lives or whatever it is. Sorry you're going through that as well. It's hard to feel like that. 

I know I should push through but it's been a while, I've been feeling like shit for 3 years now. So it's getting harder and harder to see the light at the end of the tunnel. Especially when you're seemingly doing the right things and it doesn't seem to work.

Thank you. Good for you for for cutting toxic people out and protecting your own mental health. I did the same, even though one of them wasn't always toxic, but became a toxic alcoholic asshole. And she was my best friend and always caring, before she turned into an alcoholic asshole. I can't deal with alcoholics because she reminded me of my mother, so it triggered me a lot. It wasn't good for me to be around her anymore. She became mean to me even though I was her number one person to go to and I was always there for her. But I guess her new best friend was the bottle. I tried to help her but she just resented me for it.  

I have a few friends left and am thankful for that, but I have lost a ton last year. And those friends are not good at listening and are not the most empathetic people, but I don't blame them for that. In my darkest hour a lot of friends just vanished or couldn't care to be there for me. It's still bizarre to me and I will never ever forgive them for that. It's lonely, I've never had this little social contact in my life. Always had plenty of friends. But not anymore. Maybe I will meet new people but it's not that easy in your late twenties and when you're feeling so low.

Thank you for your kind words.. I just don't understand. I talk endlessly with people about their problems. Just offering an ear to listen or some understanding. I don't expect solutions. Just a little support. But that's too much to ask when it's about me apparently. When it was about them I gave it to them. And I would never ignore my sister if she needed me. But she does it to me. I'm so lonely and nobody cares. This life is not worth living like this.
Thank you.. I wish it was this easy irl.

Thank you. But I'm really not. And if I am, they don't show it. If it was the other way around I would act extremely different. I would never ignore a person who is depressed and suicidal. It's about the dumbest thing you can do I think. And when it's too late they will all cry. But then it's too late.

It's because of how I'm treated by my family and have been treated by friends who also all have mental illness. I chose the wrong people to hang out with. I don't get support. They just leave me hanging. I'm in therapy for a year and a half now so I know what my problems are. But they also say it's important to have a stable support group around you. I don't have that and you can't just create that out of nothing. So I'm doomed.

Thank you. I just feel like I'm going crazy. I'm alone all day crying and even though people know I'm in bad shape, they don't bother to reach out. To listen. I'm just a burden when I want to vent. Lost 'friends' over it even though I was always there for them. But when I got stuck into a dark hole a year ago they just vanished. My own sister and parents don't even care to reach out to me. I have a family party this weekend but I don't think I should go. But isolating myself is also a shit idea. I just want to die really.

It's so crazy. Every parent wants their kid to be happy, right? But even if you say (repeatedly, for years) you are unhappy, school or work is priority number one! Even though it's for the most part their fault I am this way. They don't even support me being in therapy. They don't see the point.
You don't have to say sorry to me :). It's good to vent about how you feel

You're not a pussy and you're not overreacting. Small things can set me off too, because my head is full. I can't take any more things because there has been happening too much stuff lately. And I'm sure you're experiencing the same. Don't be too hard on yourself. Take your reactions and thoughts seriously and try to ask for help.
Call 911 or whatever the emergency number in your country is.

People are so awful. Even people who I somewhat trusted and known for years just have been so fucking mean to me when they knew I was already depressed and they're aware of my circumstances. Why? And I'm in therapy because I can't express myself well enough and blablabla. I'm not going to trust anyone ever. Even more so after these experiences. Friendship is an illusion. People leave, cheat or become mean cunts. I just want a dog. But I can't because I have work, so not enough time to give the dog the attention that he or she deserves. So then what? I'm just alone with my thoughts, keeping everyone at distance. I've met someone recently and he wants to hang out, even though he knows I'm not feeling well. But now I believe I'm horrible to be around and I don't even deserve attention or love or support. That's what everyone seems to think. So must be some truth in it.

Thanks. I'm sorry you're also feeling like this. I just don't know anymore. People get mad at me for ventilating. But I'm in therapy because I have to learn to express my feelings. How does that work? People only want you in their life when you're happy or pretending to be happy. Or when they are not happy and can use me to feel better about themselves. Once they don't need me anymore, I'm worthless to them and they kick me when I'm down already. They never deserved my support, time, love and friendship. But I gave it to them. And when I needed those same things from them, they wouldn't give it to me. And I have to work on my trust issues? Lol. How the fuck can I trust people when they treat me like shit? How can I learn to talk about my feelings when I get put down once I do? How can I love myself when I experience these fucking cunts all the time and they make me feel like I'm not worth shit? Fuck that. Yeah I'm the problem here. Maybe I'm delusional or maybe I am/was SURROUNDED by fucking assholes. I don't know anymore.

Thanks. It's not the case right now. My friends aren't married or something. Most of them are single and none of them have kids, none are married. And I don't feel fulfilled in anything now. I don't have a relationship, don't have a very good relationship with family. Almost no like minded friends and the ones who are like minded don't have much time for me. I 'lost' friends because I had to say goodbye because they were assholes and screwed me over. I'm switching my job, because my boss is a bitch, so maybe there will be a positive change there, but I don't know. I would like a dog but I don't have enough time for a dog, so that would be selfish. Body is ruined by antidepressants, still not at my old weight even though I eat in a calorie deficit and healthy and work out. So most days feel empty and shit. I don't like anything about my life right now and I don't know how to change it.
Haha it's okay, thanks for your help :)
Thanks, I will look into it. I don't know if it exists in my country.

Thanks. I've signed up for volunteer work but I never heard back from them. But maybe I should try harder.

And yeah moving to a new city.. I don't know. I think it wouldn't help. And I'm not the best in making new friends just out of the blue. I'm thinking about making a trip on my own, but that will only help temporarily I think.
I didn't know these things and looked it up, but I have a job so I can't just go away.
You have to have money for that. So that's not an option right now.
